 Ryan Kalkbrenner 
 CHA 
 Center 
 #11 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Ryan Kalkbrenner tallied eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 15 rebounds, three assists, two steals and three blocks in Monday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 Despite the low point total, Kalkbrenner was dominant on Monday night. Ten of his 15 rebounds came on the offensive end of the floor, and those extra opportunities helped the Hornets put up 124 points. The 7-foot-1 center, once again starting for the injured Moussa Diabaté, also recorded three assists and five defensive contributions. Kalkbrenner is worth rostering as long as the Hornets are without Diabaté. 
 Moussa Diabaté 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Moussa Diabaté (quad) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Downgraded from questionable to doubtful earlier Monday, Diabaté is now officially out. While Ryan Kalkbrenner should remain in the starting lineup, rookie Hannes Steinbach is worthy of streaming consideration for managers seeking rebounding production. 
 Moussa Diabaté 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Moussa Diabaté (quad) has been downgraded to doubtful for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Diabaté sat out Friday’s loss to Boston, and Ryan Kalkbrenner got the start. Kalkbrenner produced only four points and five rebounds across 21 minutes, while rookie Hannes Steinbach provided four points, 11 rebounds, an assist and three triples across 27 minutes off the bench. Steinbach is the preferred add, and he’s available in 98% of Yahoo! leagues.

 Coby White, Grayson Allen, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Ryan Kalkbrenner will start Friday’s game against the Celtics. 
 The Hornets are down two starters for Friday’s game: Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Moussa Diabaté (quad). Allen and Kalkbrenner will fill the resulting voids, and both are worth slotting into lineups.

 Diabaté will miss his first game of the season, which means Ryan Kalkbrenner or Naz Reid could get the start at center. Hannes Steinbach was recalled from the G League, so he could enter the rotation, too.
 Moussa Diabaté 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Moussa Diabaté (quad) is questionable to play against the Celtics on Friday. 
 Diabaté is on the injury report for the first time this season. Hannes Steinbach has been assigned to the G League, so Ryan Kalkbrenner would likely take on extra minutes down low if Diabaté is out. The Hornets could also opt to start Naz Reid at center and utilize a smaller starting unit. 
 Moussa Diabaté 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Moussa Diabaté scored 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 12 rebounds, an assist, and two steals on Friday in loss. 
 Diabaté has been as expected this season. He has value in redraft leagues if you need some rebounding, but he hasn’t done much else besides that. From a dynasty perspective, Moussa could be someone that gets moved to a new team given the surplus of centers the Hornets have, and he should have some value given his current contract. 
 Moussa Diabaté 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Moussa Diabaté recorded a double-double on Monday with 11 points (4-of-6 FGs), 17 rebounds, three assists, one steal and three blocks against the Wizards. 
 It has been a relatively quiet start to the season for Diabaté, but he was able to showcase just how good he is as a rebounder in this one. This was the third-highest rebounding total he’s had in a single game, which contributed to Charlotte’s third win of the season. Diabaté should continue to be a beast on the glass, and any other contributions in other categories are just icing on the cake.

 #24 
 Charlotte Hornets start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate in season opener against the Nets 
 The Hornets have Kon Knueppel and Coby White out, so Schroeder and now Sion James will get the start with Grayson Allen coming off the bench. Even in a start, Sion James is not a great per minute producer and will likely not impact many fantasy leagues even in a start.
